title: CardCorpus play
description: The cards that play the same, whatever their picture: one name and one text that works the same way, so an older print may stand in for a newer one in a deck. Base Set's Switch and Scarlet & Violet's are one play though their wording differs; a card that shuffles 3 cards and one that shuffles up to 3 are two. Official errata count: every Potion heals 30, so every Potion is one play. A card's `play` names this file, plays/{id}.json; only plays of more than one card have one. English cards only, for now: a translation sometimes words a card so it plays differently (https://pokemon.cardcorpus.com/v1/docs/guide.md#plays).

id.description: The play's own id: its cards' English name and a short code, such as `switch-4175`. It stays the same as cards join the play.

cardCount.description: How many cards are in it: the length of `cards`.

errata.description: The official errata its cards play by, where any do: an erratum to the name rewrites every card of it (every Potion heals 30), one to a printing corrects that printing only. Its cards whose `basis` is `errata` play by them.

scope.description: What it corrects: `name`, every card of that name; `printing`, the printing named; `rule`, a kind of card.

text.description: The corrected text, one string a paragraph, for an erratum to a name.

parts.description: For an erratum to a printing, the parts it corrects, as the card's printed text names them (`attack1 text`, `ability1 text`, `attack2 cost`, `retreat`, `effect`), with their corrected value.

change.description: What it changed, in Pokémon's words.

listed.description: When Pokémon's errata page that lists it was last updated, YYYY-MM-DD.

cards.description: Every card in it, oldest first.

items.description: A card, with what a tile draws, and the painting it prints where another card prints it too.

$kind.description: What the pointer points at: `card`. index.json's `pointers` say where to find it (https://pokemon.cardcorpus.com/v1/docs/guide.md#pointers).

id.description: The card's id, unique in its set.

name.description: A copy of the target's own `name`.

englishName.description: A copy of the target's own `englishName`.

subtitle.description: A copy of the target's own `subtitle`. The smaller name the card prints beside its own, as it prints it, in its language, where it prints one: "Professeur Chen" on a French Professor's Research, "オーキド博士" on a Japanese one. Where we have no printed subtitle, the English one on a card whose `name` is its English one (https://pokemon.cardcorpus.com/v1/docs/guide.md#subtitles).

englishSubtitle.description: A copy of the target's own `englishSubtitle`. The smaller name the card prints beside its own, in English, where it prints one: the professor on a Professor's Research ("Professor Oak"), the boss on a Boss's Orders ("Ghetsis"). It says which of the cards sharing a name this is, but isn't part of the name: a deck counts them all as one card. Always one of the card's `characters` (https://pokemon.cardcorpus.com/v1/docs/guide.md#subtitles). Our own pages show it joined to the name: "Professor's Research (Professor Oak)".

number.description: A copy of the target's own `number`. Its number as printed ("4/102", "SWSH001"), and that number without its set total.

printed.description: The number as printed, where the card prints one.

short.description: The number without its set total: "4" of "4/102", and the whole number where it prints no total ("SWSH001"). What a tile shows and a sort reads.

picture.description: A copy of the card's front picture id.

painting.description: The painting it prints, where another card prints it too.

$kind.description: What the pointer points at: `painting`. index.json's `pointers` say where to find it (https://pokemon.cardcorpus.com/v1/docs/guide.md#pointers).

id.description: The painting's own id, which never changes: its first print's English name and a short code, such as `charizard-k3f9`. Where it was first printed is `firstPrint`'s to say, corrected there when research finds an earlier print.

basis.description: Why it is in the play, from its printed text, read off its picture: `identical`, it prints the play's wording (the one most of its cards print); `wording`, it words it differently in a way that plays the same; `errata`, an official erratum (`errata`) makes it play the same; `unread`, its own text isn't read yet, so it is here by being a reprint or by its sources' text.
